daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The State Secretariat Ministry announced that the government will reduce the MBG budget and expects to complete the program's restructuring within a month, targeting needy beneficiaries more precisely. The State Secretary said thousands of overspending meal distribution points will be closed, and that MBG electric motorcycles and SPPG incentives will be restructured. The Attorney General's Office named a new suspect in MBG corruption, with revelations that suspect AYS paid money to Sony after manipulating SPPG locations.

  • The Presidential Chief of Staff stated that criticism is the breath of democracy and should not be equated with provocation.
  • The head of Indonesia's State Intelligence Agency responded to BEM SI threats of a second reform movement if the state does not improve the economy.
  • The KPK revealed that containers at Tanjung Emas Port were handled by Blueray Cargo in its ongoing investigation.
  • An ASN from BPK was detained by KPK following an OTT, claiming not to have received money.
  • PDIP's Hasto suggested President Prabowo hold a meeting on par with the 1955 Asian-African Conference.
  • Descendants of Sri Sultan Hamengku Buwono II challenged the National Hero Law at the Constitutional Court.
  • A DPR legislator said BPJS Kesehatan's Rp 2 trillion monthly deficit should not disrupt services.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia's Deputy Foreign Minister confirmed that communications with Iran continue regarding two stranded Pertamina tankers, as the strait closure persists. The Deputy FM also stated that Indonesia keeps its door open to mediate the US-Iran conflict, reiterating an earlier Prabowo offer. Indonesia is turning to African oil sources amid the Strait of Hormuz tensions, while reactivating its oil and gas assets in Venezuela to diversify supply.

  • Indonesia and South Korea will form a high-level creative industry committee to strengthen cooperation.
  • Korea Aerospace Industries stated that delivery of the KF-21 jet prototype to Indonesia awaits transfer mechanisms to be finalized.
  • Indonesia's ambassador to the United States discussed strengthening US-Indonesia library cooperation.
  • The United States supports enhanced investment and technology cooperation with Indonesia, according to diplomatic sources.
  • Indonesia and China are strengthening local currency and cross-border payment cooperation.

Other

Energy Minister Bahlil stated that Pertamax prices rose to adjust to market levels, while denying coal scarcity caused rolling blackouts. PLN apologized and disclosed current electricity supply conditions across Java. Former Vice President Jusuf Kalla and his son met President Prabowo to discuss a Rp 70 trillion energy investment.

  • Danantara leadership said the holding company safeguards assets through risk splits, distancing itself from the 1MDB scandal model.
  • State-owned enterprises contributed US$41.1 billion annually to state revenue, according to BP BUMN.
  • The government allocated US$294.1 million to develop modern agriculture in Papua.
  • The Basic and Secondary Education Minister announced that non-civil servant teacher allowances will rise to Rp 2 million.
  • The government plans to build 100 integrated national schools and will revitalize 71,744 schools this year, from kindergarten to senior high school.
